result.prompt: Select the cluster of sensory neuron cell bodies outside the spinal cord.
Follow a central process toward the cord. Select the root it travels in.
If only this root is cut, which function is directly impaired at that level?
result.chosen: Sensory input entering that side of the cord.
result.expected: Sensory input entering that side of the cord.

items.note: Sensory neuron cell bodies lie in the dorsal root ganglion. Their central processes enter by the dorsal root. Ventral roots carry motor axons.
items.title: Spinal cord segment

result.prompt: Select the mitral valve.
Select the visible ventricular muscle that tensions its chordae during systole.
If these chordae rupture, which flow can occur during ventricular systole?

items.note: Papillary muscles tension the chordae and help prevent mitral leaflet prolapse. Loss of support can allow backward flow into the left atrium.
items.title: Valve apparatus

result.prompt: Find and select any parathyroid gland.
Select the endocrine organ against whose posterior surface these glands usually lie.
As blood calcium falls, which response helps restore it?
result.chosen: PTH secretion falls and the kidneys excrete more calcium.
result.expected: PTH secretion rises and the kidneys conserve more calcium.

items.note: Parathyroid chief cells release PTH as ionized calcium falls. Renal calcium conservation and increased calcitriol production help restore extracellular calcium.
items.title: Posterior neck glands

result.prompt: Select the femoral artery.
Follow it through the adductor hiatus. Select its continuation.
Which vessel would you expect to have a weaker pulse downstream of this obstruction?
result.chosen: Dorsalis pedis on the same side.
result.expected: Dorsalis pedis on the same side.

items.note: The femoral artery becomes the popliteal artery at the adductor hiatus. Flow reaches dorsalis pedis through the anterior tibial artery distal to the knee.
items.title: Right lower-limb arteries

result.prompt: Select the incus.
Follow vibration one bone toward the oval window. Select that bone.
If the footplate becomes fixed, what change would you expect?
result.chosen: Less vibration reaches the cochlear fluid.
result.expected: Less vibration reaches the cochlear fluid.

items.note: Vibration passes from malleus to incus to stapes. The mobile stapes footplate transfers energy into the inner ear.
items.title: Middle ear

result.prompt: Select the pulmonary trunk.
Trace blood traveling toward the right lung. Select the next artery.
After blood exchanges gases in that lung, which chamber receives it first?

items.note: Blood travels from the right ventricle through the pulmonary trunk and pulmonary arteries. Pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood to the left atrium.
items.title: Pulmonary vessels

result.prompt: Select the cerebral aqueduct.
Follow CSF through this channel and select the cavity it enters next.
If only this channel closes, which spaces can enlarge upstream?

items.note: CSF passes from the third ventricle through the aqueduct into the fourth. A block can enlarge the lateral and third ventricles.
items.title: Ventricular system

result.prompt: Select the right adrenal gland.
Select the organ just inferior to this gland on the same side.
A fall in aldosterone most directly reduces which renal response?
result.chosen: Sodium reabsorption in the late distal nephron.
result.expected: Sodium reabsorption in the late distal nephron.

items.note: Aldosterone from the adrenal cortex promotes renal sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in the aldosterone-sensitive distal nephron.
items.title: Posterior abdominal wall
